notes:
Final read-only review of PR #627 at exact head b3800e42503d2ae709195dda58cb2e8a1fdc6352. Effective profile: rules-clause-complete. Reviewed the complete origin/main...HEAD diff (18 files) and seven-commit history; live owning, dispatch, prior-review and repair beads; AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md; applicable ADRs 0011/0012/0015/0018/0020 and class-resource authority in docs/design/character-progression.md; importer protocol applicability; vendored SRD 5.1 pp. 42-44 and generated Font of Magic procedure. Traced real producers/consumers through the usage/slot owners, model-facing tools and registry, prompt, context assembly and orchestrator, rests, progression, transaction rollback, replay and checkpoint serialization. No importer or generated-pack records change. refs/beads/state is stale (generated 2026-09-10) and lacks these beads; reconciled with live bd records.

Prior findings: eshyra-09co.2 S1's Flexible Casting alias/legacy adoption is repaired. eshyra-09co.4 S1's resolver drift is repaired by a shared memo per Flexible Casting operation; S2's restore_usage normalization is repaired. eshyra-09co.6 S1's class/procedure disagreement is repaired by atomic rejection plus persisted-delta assertion. S2's finite-capacity reset/rest normalization is repaired, but the shared active-economy obligation remains incomplete in the following concrete paths. This was a fresh full review of the affected subsystem, as required by the churn rule, rather than an example-only recheck.

S1 — MATERIAL (P1): packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts:641-645 (changed reader boundary :364 and :571; real caller orchestrator.ts:832-843). assembleContext accepts input.resolveRulesPack but does not forward it to readStateSnapshot, whose new readSpentUsageCounters path now resolves the active class stack. Concrete scenario reproduced with real APIs: store a valid level-3 sorcerer, bind a supported class add-on with sorceryPoints maximum 4, and supply its resolver to assembleContext. Context succeeds before expenditure. spendUsage with that resolver consumes one point and correctly reports maximum 4; readSpentUsageCounters(db, campaignId, resolver) also succeeds. The next assembleContext call with the SAME resolver throws UsageCounterError: "cannot resolve class resource capacity: campaign rules pack ... is unavailable", because the snapshot call drops the resolver. The orchestrator calls this during assemble_context before the DM call, so normal play cannot continue after that spend. Identical probes fail for Ki and Rage. No malformed state, resolver drift, or database counter edits are required. Authority: supported campaign base/add-on resolution contract, the accepted eshyra-09co.7 context sweep, ADR 0012 mechanical truth, and the current orchestrator/ContextAssemblyInput resolver contract. Suggested fix (owner: context assembly): pass input.resolveRulesPack into readStateSnapshot and keep the snapshot/resource view and campaign-rules context on the same resolved source, using the existing turn memo; preserve existing binding failure behavior. Permanent evidence: a generalized integration invariant through assembleContext (or the actual turn path) that a resolvable non-bundled binding remains usable before and after a selected-resource spend and presents its active capacity; cover the shared Sorcery Points/Ki/Rage boundary. Small in-memory integration evidence is proportionate to a normal-turn blocker.

S2 — MATERIAL (P2): packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:1917-1940 (especially :1931-1936; consumer contextAssembler.ts:571 and formatUsageCounter at :1949). The new read-only overlay changes only maximum/used on each raw row; it does not implement the resource owner's canonical alias adoption, most-spent duplicate rule, reset/source/name normalization, or none/unlimited disposition. Concrete real-pack legacy scenario reproduced entirely through existing APIs: before storing the sheet, spendUsage creates Font of Magic with declared maximum 9, short_rest reset, used 3, and sorcery-points with maximum 3, long_rest reset, used 1. Store a valid level-3 sorcerer sheet. readSpentUsageCounters now returns BOTH pools: Font of Magic 3/3 used (resets on a short rest), and sorcery-points 1/3 used (resets on a long rest), both source declared. The real owner treats these aliases as ONE pool with most-spent used=3; registered flexible_casting create-slot level 1 correctly refuses because zero points remain. Thus context presents two contradictory balances and a false short-rest recovery rule despite knowing the active binding. Sibling capacity scenario: a valid level-20 barbarian spends all six Rages under a supported finite-capacity class add-on, then the campaign binding returns to the bundled table's Unlimited at 20. assembleContext still renders "Rage 6/6 used (resets on a long rest)" while spendUsage succeeds with unlimited=true. These do not depend on S1; the legacy case uses only the bundled binding, and the Unlimited case removes the add-on before reading. The same row-by-row mechanism affects Ki aliases and leaves none-capacity rows advertised as finite resources. Authority: docs/design/character-progression.md selected-resource/alias/reset/Unlimited contracts, accepted eshyra-09co.7 read/report normalization invariant, and ADR 0020 truthful resource accounting before adjudication. Suggested fix (owner: counter read projection): build a nonmutating canonical projection equivalent to the counter owner's reconciliation: group aliases per character/resource, use the most-spent expenditure clamped to active finite capacity, normalize canonical key/display/reset/source, and omit or explicitly represent unavailable/unlimited resources instead of emitting stale finite counters. Preserve other counters and keep reads nonmutating. Permanent evidence: a generalized invariant that the read-only view of canonical, alias-only and duplicate legacy representations agrees with the owner's effective pool/reset/source without changing stored rows, including finite, none and Unlimited transitions. This small boundary matrix is proportionate to incorrect model-visible resource balances and recovery instructions.

S3 — MATERIAL (P2): packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:1785 (downstream reset selection/mutation :1835-1880; rest consumers state/rest.ts:702 and :720). When the active class table provides no finite capacity, reconcileScopeBoundCounters skips the resource but resetUsage subsequently selects and refills the unchanged stale row. Concrete supported-binding scenario reproduced for Sorcery Points, Ki and Rage: spend one use at level 3 under the bundled table, then bind a class-only add-on whose level-3 resourceProgression entry for that resource is absent. spendUsage with that resolver correctly refuses "has no ... at level 3 per the class table; nothing to spend". Nevertheless resetUsage long_rest succeeds and reports/persists usesMax=3, usesUsed=0, usesRemaining=3; completeLongRest with the same binding likewise returns those three restored uses in usageReset. No direct counter mutations are involved. Preserving a historical row during level-up does not authorize a reset to replenish/report a finite economy the active table does not supply. Authority: the accepted eshyra-09co.7 active maximum/reset/source and none-handling invariant, docs/design/character-progression.md's absent-capacity refusal and named reset_usage consumer, and ADR 0020 state integrity. Suggested fix (owner: reset/rest integration): prevent none-capacity bound rows from entering the reset mutation and successful recovery results; retain their historical expenditure without refilling it, or refuse the affected operation atomically. Keep this decision consistent with the read projection and existing spend/restore refusal, while preserving owner and event scopes. Permanent evidence: a generalized invariant that reset_usage and actual rest recovery cannot refill or report a stale finite selected-resource pool after the active capacity becomes none, covering canonical/alias forms and the shared resource bindings. Small in-memory tests distinguish a genuinely unavailable economy from finite-capacity reconciliation.

Verification: 12 targeted files passed, 374 tests (flexibleCasting, classResourceActiveCapacity, spellSlots, usageCounters, rest, spellUpcast, contextAssembler, contextAssemblerParty, tools, persistence, migrationLegacyAdoption, migrationRunner). Six levelUpEngine class-resource tests and one source-derived Font of Magic evaluator test also passed; remaining tests in those two files were excluded by explicit name filters. Used existing parent-resolved dependencies from this worktree, with native Vitest config loading and cache disabled. Independent stdin probes used only in-memory databases, reproduced S1-S3, and checked the Font of Magic cost table and maxima against the vendored source, a created level-5 slot above the class progression with registered spend_spell_slot upcasting, real context visibility, replay restoration, actual short-rest preservation/long-rest expiry and point reset, and atomic missing-slot refusal. git diff --check passed; final worktree status clean at the assigned SHA. No repository edits, install/build/format/verify, GitHub writes, commits, pushes or merges.

No non-material findings recorded. Automatic bonus-action consumption: no requirement in this PR, because the original dispatch explicitly assigns it to the DM/existing turn-resource tool. A special flexible_casting error code for a feature override lacking a bounded procedure: no requirement; the registry returns a clear tool_error and the transaction rolls back. Required next state: repair S1-S3 and freshly review the resulting exact head before merge. Only this review bead is closed; eshyra-09co remains untouched.
